Scientific Hypothesis: In developing countries, increased education expenditure is positively correlated with economic output indicators such as exports of goods and services and labor force participation rate. This relationship suggests that higher investment in education may lead to improved economic performance, as reflected in these indicators. The correlation coefficients between education expenditure and exports, as well as education expenditure and labor force participation rate, are approximately 0.586, indicating a moderate positive relationship.
